intro: The Wetherspoons burger menu has {itemCount} choices, with typical prices from {minPrice} to {maxPrice} and {vegCount} vegetarian or vegan options. overview.heading: What beef burgers does Wetherspoons serve?
overview.body:
The beef selection runs from the classic beef burger to double-patty options with cheese and bacon. The classic combines a beef patty with lettuce, tomato and red onion, making it the straightforward starting point. The [American Cheese Burger](/burgers/american-cheese-burger) changes the flavour profile with American-style cheese, gherkins, ketchup and mustard. For something sweeter and smokier, the [BBQ Bacon Burger](/burgers/bbq-bacon-burger) adds cheddar, maple-cured bacon and BBQ sauce.

The [Double American Cheese Burger](/burgers/double-american-cheese-burger) uses two beef patties and double cheese, while the Empire State Burger combines two patties with American-style cheese and maple-cured bacon. Choose between them by toppings as well as appetite: the double cheese option has gherkins and mustard, whereas the Empire State emphasises cheese and bacon.

overview.heading: Which Wetherspoons chicken burger should you choose?
overview.body:
The chicken burgers differ chiefly in their coating and side, so those are the useful details to compare first. The Fried Buttermilk Chicken Burger has a chicken breast marinated in buttermilk and covered in seasoned breading, with lettuce, tomato and mayonnaise. It suits someone who specifically wants a crunchy coating rather than a grilled breast.

The Grilled Chicken Breast Burger comes in a toasted bun with lettuce and tomato, accompanied by chips. The Skinny Chicken Burger also uses grilled chicken but replaces the chips with a side salad. That is a clear change in meal format, not a reason to assume a particular calorie saving. If [nutrition](/nutrition-information) is your priority, check the current figures for the complete serving.

overview.heading: Which Wetherspoons burgers are vegetarian or vegan?
overview.body:
The Beyond Meat Plant-Based Burger and Fiesta Burger carry both vegan and vegetarian tags, while the Breaded Vegetable Burger is tagged vegetarian. The Beyond Meat option uses a plant-based patty in a bun with lettuce and tomato. Fiesta builds on a Beyond Meat patty with roasted red peppers, courgettes and onions, making the vegetable toppings its clearest point of difference.

The Breaded Vegetable Burger takes a different approach, with lentils, carrots and sweetcorn inside a breadcrumb coating. It is the choice to consider if you prefer a vegetable-based filling rather than a patty described as resembling beef. Do not assume the vegetarian option is also vegan: use the current dietary labelling and ask about the complete serving before ordering.

overview.heading: Do Wetherspoons burger choices change by pub?
overview.body:
No seasonal or rotating burger is identified in the supplied menu information, so this guide cannot name a confirmed special or promise the full selection at your pub. The named choices cover classic beef, cheese and bacon combinations, chicken, and plant-based fillings. Use that range as your starting point, then check the current local menu rather than expecting an additional seasonal item.

If your first choice cannot be ordered, look for the closest match by format. Compare the two American cheese options for a cheese-led beef burger, or the grilled and skinny chicken options when the side matters most. Plant-based diners should check the replacement's own dietary label, rather than assuming that an alternative topping or substitution keeps the meal vegan.

allergenSummary:
Buns, breading, cheese, buttermilk and mustard are the main ingredient clues to check for burger allergens. Consult Wetherspoons' current allergen information for cereals containing gluten, milk and mustard, and check the egg status of mayonnaise rather than relying on the descriptions here. The supplied information is not a complete breakdown of the fourteen major allergens.

Tell staff about your allergy before ordering and do not rely on this independent guide alone. Ask about the entire meal, including the bun, sauces and side. If requesting a swap or omission, confirm how it affects allergen information and ask about shared kitchen equipment and cross-contact. A dietary tag does not establish suitability for someone with an allergy.
